Player Hater
PLAY-er HAY-ter
noun (Gen X slang)
A hip-hop compound of the mid-1990s (also playa hater, verb playa-hatin’): one who resents and runs down another person’s success, style, or popularity. The Notorious B.I.G. recorded "Playa Hater" on Life After Death (1997), and the phrase was later lampooned in the "Player Haters’ Ball" sketches on Chappelle’s Show (2003). Shortened by the end of the 1990s to hater.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

A player hater is someone who cannot stand to see another man do well: he mocks the new car, sneers at the girlfriend, whispers about the promotion. The slang assumed the success was admirable and the hater was small — and on the second point Scripture agrees completely. The sin underneath is envy, and the Bible is unsparing about it. "A sound heart is the life of the flesh: but envy the rottenness of the bones" (Pro 14:30). "Where envying and strife is, there is confusion and every evil work" (Jas 3:16). Solomon saw that much of the world’s labor is driven by it: "for this a man is envied of his neighbour. This is also vanity and vexation of spirit" (Ecc 4:4). Paul warns believers not to be "provoking one another, envying one another" (Gal 5:26). Here the Bible adds something the slang missed. Asaph confessed, "I was envious at the foolish, when I saw the prosperity of the wicked" (Psa 73:3). Sometimes the "player" being hated is not admirable at all — and the believer’s temptation is to envy him anyway, to wish he had the playa’s freedom. "Let not thine heart envy sinners: but be thou in the fear of the LORD all the day long" (Pro 23:17). The cure for both kinds of envy is the same: go into the sanctuary, as Asaph did, and see the end of things; then rejoice with them that rejoice. A father can tell his son: don’t be a hater, and don’t envy the playa — love your brother’s good, and want God more than anything anyone else has.

Webster 1828 Definition

Mid-1990s hip-hop compound (Notorious B.I.G., "Playa Hater," 1997) for one who resents another’s success; Scripture names the sin envy, the rottenness of the bones (Pro 14:30), and warns too against envying sinners (Psa 73:3).

PLAYER HATER, n. (Gen X slang, mid-1990s, hip-hop) One who resents, mocks, or undermines another’s success, style, or popularity. "Don’t listen to him — he’s just a player hater."

Variants: playa hater; verb playa-hatin’; shortened to hater by the late 1990s.

The Notorious B.I.G., "Playa Hater" (Life After Death, 1997); Chappelle’s Show, "Player Haters’ Ball" (2003).

Webster 1828: HATER, n. One that hates. An enemy to God, and hater of all good.

Decode for parents: "player hater" names envy; teach your children to rejoice in others’ good and to envy no one, least of all sinners.

Key Scripture

Pro 14:30 — "A sound heart is the life of the flesh: but envy the rottenness of the bones."

Jas 3:16 — "For where envying and strife is, there is confusion and every evil work."

Ecc 4:4 — "Again, I considered all travail, and every right work, that for this a man is envied of his neighbour. This is also vanity and vexation of spirit."

Gal 5:26 — "Let us not be desirous of vain glory, provoking one another, envying one another."

Psa 73:3 — "For I was envious at the foolish, when I saw the prosperity of the wicked."

Modern Corruption

Player hater rightly mocks envy but assumes the player is worth envying; Scripture condemns envy at its root and warns the believer not to envy sinners at all.

expand to see more

Envy named, envy kept. The phrase was a clever defense: any criticism of the player could be waved off as hating. That made envy easy to name in others and hard to see in oneself, and it shielded the player from honest rebuke. Scripture does not let either side off. Envy rots the bones (Pro 14:30) and breeds confusion and every evil work (Jas 3:16); but a man’s success does not make his life right, and a friend’s warning is not hate.

Asaph’s cure. Psalm 73 is the Bible’s honest account of player-hating: a godly man nearly slipped because he envied the prosperity of the wicked (Psa 73:3). His cure was not to stop noticing but to go into the sanctuary of God and understand their end. A believer freed from envy can do what the hater cannot — rejoice with them that rejoice — because charity envieth not (1Co 13:4) and his treasure is safe in God.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Street player + English hater → mid-1990s hip-hop player hater → Biggie’s "Playa Hater" (1997) → hater → Chappelle’s "Player Haters’ Ball" (2003); Scripture: envy the rottenness of the bones (Pro 14:30).
